quizName: Hardest Questions in New jersey Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What helps reduce head or neck injury risk in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to prevent head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Eyeballing the tire is a good method.
It is best to squeeze the tire.
Compare the height of the tire to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. Looking at the tire is not enough because under-inflated tires may still look normal.

questions.question: Why should you wear a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket made of leather for protection. Modern motorcycle jackets keep you cool even in warm weather.

questions.question: Where should you find information specific to your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before riding it for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you check before every ride?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before each ride, inspect your tires, oil, fluid levels, lights, turn signals, brakes, mirrors, and horn.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made from?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: What should you do if you can't avoid a slippery surface?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: If your footwear has laces, what should you do with them?

options.text: Should be taken off of the footwear.

questions.explanation: Tuck in your laces securely so they don't catch on the motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly. Always check them before changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may unexpectedly pull out from the row into your path.
Others may be driving slowly while looking for a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may unexpectedly pull out from the row into your path.
questions.explanation: A driver might pull out of a parking space without looking. Car doors may open into your lane and pedestrians may step out between cars.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal plates are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: Where should you get main information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It has details about how it works, how to operate it, and what maintenance it needs.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different, so be careful with an unfamiliar one. Learn how it works before you ride. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes, and learn the gear pattern.

questions.question: Which organization certifies helmets for maximum protection?
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles
They alert other motorists to what you plan to do
They should only be used when other vehicles are close
They are more complicated than signals on cars

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other motorists to what you plan to do
questions.explanation: As a motorcyclist, you are especially vulnerable. Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do. Use them whenever you change lanes or turn, even if no one seems nearby.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up
Get off the road and rest

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest
questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riding clothes cover?

options.text: Your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed
Your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed
Whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety

questions.explanation: For proper protection while riding, wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: What type of boots or shoes provide the best protection for riding?

options.text: Boots or shoes made of soft material
Boots or shoes with long laces that are not tucked in
Boots or shoes that cover the ankle and provide support
Boots or shoes with tall heels

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots or shoes that cover the ankle and provide support
questions.explanation: Choose boots or heavy shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they do not catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Encourage them to take roads that are not crowded

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Do whatever is needed to stop them, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a motorcycle crash?

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the single most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what kind of clothing should you wear?

options.text: Loose clothing that flaps in the wind.
Clothing that leaves your arms or legs uncovered.
Clothing that protects you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that protects you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and long pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothes should fit snugly so they don't flap, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What should you look for in a helmet?

options.text: It meets Department of Transportation rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: It meets Department of Transportation rules.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks or damage.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright colors, keep your headlight on at all times, and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: Which color is best for being seen on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible. Bright colors help others see you anytime you ride.

questions.question: What brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in and not be noticed.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by being visible to others. Signal your turns and lane changes, use your brake light, and stay in the right lane position. Keep space around your bike, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to problems.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Tell them to take quiet roads.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: Which of these does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, ankle-high boots or shoes, and durable gloves to protect yourself.

questions.question: Why is keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles important?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one spot in your lane.
It lets you rely on other drivers to spot problems.
It means you can ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle helps you have time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles. Laced boots work best. If you wear shoes with long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:
questions.explanation: Wear riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to help you grip the handlebars better.
Not be worn because they make it hard to use the controls.
Be worn only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to help you grip the handlebars better.
questions.explanation: Wear gloves made of leather or other durable material. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: To get the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no visible damage.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is around to see it.

questions.question: To get the most protection when choosing a helmet, use one that:

options.text: Has been in a previous crash.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the most protection. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: For safe riding, wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your blood alcohol content (BAC). Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Always wear bright-colored clothing to be more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: Which of the following surfaces provides the best traction for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces provide poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are more hazardous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Which of the following does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. A small problem on a motorcycle can be very dangerous in traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good protective gear includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface that makes it hard to control a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride with extra caution on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You can cross into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You usually stay in your lane.
It is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can make you cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly lowers your risk of serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to sobering up.

questions.question: The best gear to wear when you ride is:

options.text: Any gear that helps protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you. Use a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers see you.
Are only needed in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often for safety. Regular mirror checks should be part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to reach and operate the controls easily.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.
